description: Shopware 6 is an open commerce platform based on Symfony Framework and Vue and supported by a worldwide community and more than 3.100 community extensions
vibe: Guard the shared test kernel, prove the work ran, and never let a skill be optional when CI depends on it.
highlights: Explicitly warns that Twig-only template changes must never get PHP integration tests, because rendering without a Storefront request can cache empty request-dependent Twig globals in the shared test kernel and break unrelated later tests.
Mandates that a CI job must never report success without proving the work ran, with local rules in .github/AGENTS.md.
States that skills are best-effort and model-decided, not guaranteed, so mandatory steps are duplicated in the always-loaded file.
Enforces a Definition of Done with behavior-change-implies-tests, conventional commit scopes, follow-up commits after review instead of amend/force-push, and linting every touched file.
Codifies Shopware's non-Symfony architecture: no Doctrine ORM, no QueryBuilder, no annotations, no Doctrine repositories; prefer events over decorators.
assessment: This file shows unusually mature agent-instruction design: it treats skill triggering as probabilistic and therefore hoists non-negotiable rules into the always-loaded context, which is exactly the right failure model for LLM agents. The Twig/test-kernel warning is a rare, concrete piece of institutional knowledge that prevents a subtle class of cross-test contamination, and the CI 'must prove the work ran' rule encodes a strong anti-greenwashing stance. The result is a defensive but pragmatic contract that keeps agent output aligned with a large, BC-sensitive open-source codebase.
